content.text: Section 14 fully implements the preferred position, so no redline is needed.

input.quote: 14.2 Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel. Vendor will execute further documents reasonably needed to confirm ownership.
input.rationale: The IP package meets our preferred position in full. § 14.1 confirms Customer owns Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information and Customer-provided and pre-existing IP, with no transfer to Vendor beyond a processing right limited to delivering the Services for us; § 15.1 reinforces this by barring sale, advertising use, data combination and model training without our written consent. § 14.2 vests ownership of each Deliverable in Customer on creation with a present assignment, personnel assignments and further-assurance covenant. § 14.3 lets Vendor keep only Vendor Technology (defined in § 1.8 to exclude Customer Data and our pre-existing IP) and channels embedded Vendor Technology into the § 13.2 perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, modify, create derivative works and permit contractor support for our business — the licence-back the rule requires. § 14.4 expressly negates joint ownership absent a signed instrument setting exploitation rights, and keeps our unrestricted right to use our own feedback. The only mild narrowing is that § 1.4 ties Deliverables to items an Order Form identifies as created specifically for Customer, which is ordinary scoping we manage at the Order Form level and does not warrant a redline on a compliant clause set.
